lines.text: Practice — Apply
PRACTICE
Ira eats biscuits, white bread and noodles, and avoids vegetables and fruit.
She often has stomach ache and difficulty passing stool.
Which component is missing from her diet?
Name three foods she should add, and explain what each will do.
Reshma has trouble seeing in dim light. Her doctor prescribes a vitamin
supplement and advises a change of diet.
(i) Which deficiency disorder does she most likely have?
(ii) Which nutrient is short in her diet?
(iii) Name four foods she should include.
Gourav fractures his leg. His doctor sets the bone, applies a plaster, and
prescribes calcium tablets. At the next visit the doctor adds Vitamin D syrup.
Use Fig. 3.5 to answer:
(i) Why calcium?
(ii) Why add Vitamin D alongside it, rather than more calcium?
(iii) What question would you want to ask the doctor?
You are offered canned fruit juice, freshly squeezed juice, and a whole
fresh fruit. Which would you choose, and why?
Give two reasons, at least one of them about a nutrient.
Sugar is a carbohydrate, but sugar tested with iodine does not turn blue-black.
What does this tell you about the relationship between sugar and starch?
A drop of iodine solution falls on Ira's cotton socks and another on her
teacher's silk saree. The drop on the saree turns blue-black; the drop on
the socks does not. Suggest an explanation. (Think about what is used to
stiffen cloth.)
A family lives in a district where the soil is low in iodine. They eat plenty of
locally grown food and are not short of meals. Explain why a member of that
family might still develop goitre, and what the simplest remedy would be.
Two snacks weigh the same. One lists 8 g protein and 3 g fibre per 100 g;
the other lists 3 g protein and 1 g fibre, with twice the fat.
Which is the better everyday snack?
Justify your answer using the numbers.
